input.content:
Commit 9184f9d. All reads went through `git show` / `git grep` at that commit. I opened 14 of the 15 budgeted files: the 13 assigned (4 of them templates) plus a slice of `roombooker/rooms/service.py`. `roombooker/core/db.py` and `roombooker/people/service.py` were seen only as grep hits.

## Storage and schema
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: `start_at` and `end_at` are NOT NULL strings, with CHECK `end_at > start_at` (`ck_bookings_end_after_start`). This rejects any row whose end is not after its start.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:58-59 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: the only indexes are `(room_id, start_at)` and `(organiser_id)`. There is no index containing `end_at`.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: `booking_attendees.booking_id` uses ON DELETE CASCADE, so removing a booking also removes its attendees. This depends on `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` at `roombooker/core/db.py:15 @ 9184f9d` (grep hit only).
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`: the Table describes `end_at` as String.

## Overlap guard (load-bearing)
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`, **load-bearing**. It aborts with `room_closed` if the room's `is_closed` is set. It aborts with `booking_conflict` if another booking in the same room satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`. That is a half-open interval test, and it excludes the row itself via `other.id IS NOT NEW.id`.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:77-83 @ 9184f9d`: `_GUARD` runs BEFORE INSERT, and BEFORE UPDATE OF `room_id, start_at, end_at`. No Python code issues an UPDATE on bookings: the store has only `insert` and `delete_booking`.

## Removal paths (load-bearing)
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings) @ 9184f9d`, **load-bearing**. AFTER UPDATE OF `is_closed` on rooms, when a room goes from open to closed, it runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE room_id = NEW.id AND start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`.
  - The filter is on `start_at`, not `end_at`. A booking that is in progress, or already finished, survives the close.
  - "now" includes real seconds, while stored times always end in `:00Z`.
- `roombooker/rooms/service.py:205-219 (_set_closed, close_room) @ 9184f9d`: `close_room` → `store.set_closed` → commit. It does no booking deletion in Python; the docstring points to the trigger.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`: this is the only Python DELETE on bookings, by id. A grep for `DELETE FROM|delete(` across `*.py`, excluding tests, found only this and the trigger.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:353-361 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`, **load-bearing**. It raises `NotAllowed(ONLY_ORGANISER)` if the viewer is not the organiser, and `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` if `view.end_at <= clock.utc_now()`.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`: calls `booking_to_cancel` (the end-time check) first, then `begin_immediate`, then `delete_booking`, then commit. The end-time check runs before the write lock is taken.
- `roombooker/bookings/web.py:299-314 (confirm_cancel) @ 9184f9d`: GET calls `booking_to_cancel`, so the end check applies, and renders `details.html` with `has_ended=False`.
- `roombooker/bookings/web.py:317-322 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`: POST calls `service.cancel`, then redirects to `/rooms?notice=cancelled`.

## Queries that filter on end_at
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:45-51 (overlapping) @ 9184f9d`: any room where `start_at < end_at_param AND end_at > start_at_param`, ordered by `start_at, id`.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`: `organiser_id == id AND end_at > after`, with LIMIT.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:66-80 (for_person) @ 9184f9d`: the same overlap test as `overlapping`, restricted to bookings the person organises or attends (subquery on `booking_attendees`).
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:83-84 (get) @ 9184f9d`: fetch by id. Through `service._get_row` (`service.py:267-271`) it becomes `BookingNotFound` (404) when the row is missing or the id is outside 1..2^63-1.

## Service call sites
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:107-120 (check_slot) @ 9184f9d`, **load-bearing**. It computes the end as `start + length`. It rejects:
  - a start that is not on a quarter hour (`NOT_ON_QUARTER`)
  - a length outside 15–240 minutes or not a multiple of 15 (`BAD_LENGTH`)
  - a start before now, unless `allow_past` (`IN_THE_PAST`)
  - a start more than 90 days ahead (`TOO_FAR_AHEAD`)

  It does not check the end against now.
- `service.py:123-148 (free_rooms) @ 9184f9d`: takes the end from `check_slot`, runs `store.overlapping` to build the set of taken room ids, and also drops closed rooms in Python (line 136).
- `service.py:151-188 (_views) @ 9184f9d`: `end_at = clock.from_text(row.end_at)` (line 170) and puts it in `BookingView.end_at`. Every view-producing path goes through here. It looks up `rooms[row.room_id]` from `all_rooms`, which includes closed rooms.
- `service.py:191-197 (bookings_in_slot) @ 9184f9d`: end is `start + length` computed directly, without `check_slot`, then `store.overlapping` → `_views`.
- `service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`: `store.upcoming_for_organiser(after=utc_now(), limit=20)`. A booking stays listed until its end passes.
- `service.py:208-214 (bookings_for_person) @ 9184f9d`: `store.for_person` → `_views`.
- `service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d`: returns the closed message if the room is closed (checked before `check_slot`). Otherwise it calls `check_slot` and returns the taken message if `store.overlapping` has a row in this room. It describes itself as advisory only.
- `service.py:279-282 (booking_calendar) @ 9184f9d`: `get_booking` → `ical.calendar([view])`. There is no ended or closed filter.
- `service.py:285-290 (feed_calendar) @ 9184f9d`: `bookings_for_person(now - 30 days, FEED_END)`, where `FEED_END = 9999-12-31T23:59Z` (line 35). The feed therefore holds bookings whose end is after 30 days ago.
- `service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d`, **load-bearing**. It computes the end with `check_slot` (line 316), then `begin_immediate` → `store.insert(... to_text(end_at) ...)`. It maps an IntegrityError containing `room_closed` to `RoomClosed` (409) and one containing `booking_conflict` to `BookingConflict` (409); any other IntegrityError is re-raised. It raises `InvalidBooking(ATTENDEE_GONE)` for an inactive attendee.
- `roombooker/calendar/service.py:18-22 (my_bookings) @ 9184f9d`: passes straight through to `bookings_for_person`.
- `roombooker/calendar/service.py:25-31 (feed) @ 9184f9d`: token → person, or None → `feed_calendar`.

## iCal
- `roombooker/bookings/ical.py:52-64 (uid) @ 9184f9d`: the UID hash covers the room id, `start_at`, `end_at` and title. Changing the end time produces a different UID, so calendar apps treat it as a new event rather than an update.
- `ical.py:67-79 (_event) @ 9184f9d`: writes `DTEND:{clock.ical_utc(booking.end_at)}` (line 73) and always `STATUS:CONFIRMED`.

## Web call sites
- `roombooker/bookings/web.py:76-78 (_slot_text) @ 9184f9d`: end is `start + length`, shown as a UK clock time. Used at lines 121 and 152.

input.content:
The two kinds of trigger use different rules. The overlap guard counts **every booking row in the room**, past, current and future, and checks nothing about time. The close trigger deletes only rows whose `start_at` is strictly later than SQLite's own clock. "Removed" has no column: cancelled bookings are deleted rows, so they simply stop counting.

Citations are `path:line (symbol) @ 9184f9d`. **[LB]** marks the load-bearing claims.

**1. Overlap guard (`bookings_no_overlap_insert` / `bookings_no_overlap_update`)**
- **[LB]** Both triggers run the same `_GUARD` body: `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:77-79` (upgrade, BEFORE INSERT) and `:80-83` (upgrade, `BEFORE UPDATE OF room_id, start_at, end_at`).
- **[LB]** Check 1 aborts with `room_closed` when `rooms.is_closed` is true for `NEW.room_id`: `0003_bookings.py:24-25 (_GUARD)`. It runs before the overlap check, so a booking in a closed room reports `room_closed` even if it also overlaps.
  - `is_closed` is a non-null Boolean defaulting to false: `migrations/versions/0002_rooms.py:31 (upgrade)`.
  - If the room id doesn't exist, the subquery returns NULL and the guard does not abort. The `fk_bookings_room_id_rooms` foreign key (`0003_bookings.py:44`) catches that instead, with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` from `roombooker/core/db.py:15 (PRAGMAS)`.
- **[LB]** Check 2 aborts with `booking_conflict` when any other booking in the same room overlaps. The rule is `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`, which treats intervals as half-open, so back-to-back bookings are allowed: `0003_bookings.py:26-33 (_GUARD)`.
  - `other.id IS NOT NEW.id` stops an UPDATE from colliding with its own row. On INSERT, `NEW.id` is usually NULL, so every row counts: `:30`.
  - **[LB]** There is no condition on time or status. A finished booking still blocks an overlapping new one. The only way a booking stops counting is deletion.
- The comparison is plain text. That works because times are stored as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`, so text order is time order (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:4-5`, module docstring), plus `ck_bookings_end_after_start` (`0003_bookings.py:56`).
- At this commit no app code updates `bookings`. A git grep for `UPDATE|update(` in `roombooker/bookings` found nothing. Writes are only `store.insert` (`store.py:94-115`) and `delete_booking` (`store.py:118-120`), so the UPDATE trigger never fires from the app.

**2. How a trigger abort reaches the user (`book`)**
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book)`: `begin_immediate` (`:326`, defined at `store.py:35-42`), then the insert. An `IntegrityError` is rolled back and mapped by substring: `room_closed` becomes `RoomClosed` (`:344-345`), `booking_conflict` becomes `BookingConflict` (`:346-347`), and anything else is re-raised (`:348`).
- Before the trigger, `check_slot(start_at, length_minutes, allow_past)` at `:316` rejects some slots; past slots are refused unless `allow_past` is set (only the seed sets it, per the docstring at `:313-314`). I did not open `check_slot`. Because of it, past bookings come from the seed but are still counted by the guard.

**3. The advisory duplicate in Python (`slot_problem`)**
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem)` runs the same two checks before the database does:
  - `room.is_closed` returns the closed message (`:234-235`).
  - `store.overlapping` fetches overlapping rows in **any** room using the same half-open test (`store.py:45-51`, `overlapping`, `start_at < end_at AND end_at > start_at`), then Python filters to the room (`:238`).
- It has no time or status filter either. The docstring says it is advisory and that the triggers remain the guarantee (`:231-232`).

**4. Close cascade (`rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings`)**
- **[LB]** `0003_bookings.py:86-93 (upgrade)`: `AFTER UPDATE OF is_closed ON rooms` with `WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`. It fires only when a room goes from open to closed. Reopening, or closing an already-closed room, deletes nothing.
- **[LB]** What it deletes: `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE room_id = NEW.id AND start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')` (`:90-92`).
  - "Future" means `start_at` is strictly after the database clock.
  - A booking in progress (`start_at <= now < end_at`) is kept, and so are past bookings.
  - A booking starting at exactly the current second is kept, because the test is `>` not `>=`.
  - `strftime` includes real seconds, while stored values always end in `:00Z`. Both strings are the same length, so the text comparison still works.
- It uses SQLite's `'now'`, not `core.time.utc_now()`. The ADR names this as a trade-off: a fake clock in tests can't move it (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:7`).
- Attendee rows go with the deleted bookings through `ondelete="CASCADE"` (`0003_bookings.py:65-66`), which also depends on `foreign_keys=ON` (`core/db.py:15`).
- Call path:
  - `roombooker/rooms/service.py:215-218 (close_room)` calls `_set_closed(..., is_closed=True)` (`:205-212`). Its only Python-side check is `_require_manager` (`:208`).
    - `roombooker/rooms/store.py:49-50 (set_closed)` runs `UPDATE rooms SET is_closed`, which fires the trigger in the same statement; the commit is at `rooms/service.py:210`.
- The ADR states the intended rule: future bookings are deleted, while in-progress and past ones stay (`adr...md:3`). It also says a booking racing the close cannot survive it. Either the booking commits first and the trigger deletes it, or the close commits first and the overlap guard refuses it with `room_closed` (`adr...md:3`).

**5. "Removed" bookings**
- There is no soft-delete or status column. The `bookings` columns are id, room_id, organiser_id, title, start_at and end_at (`0003_bookings.py:38-57`; `store.py:16-25`).
- A git grep in `roombooker` and `migrations` for `status|cancelled_at|deleted_at|removed` found only HTTP status codes, the iCal `STATUS:CONFIRMED` line and an unrelated web variable. The migrations directory has 0001 to 0004 and none adds such a column (0004 I saw by filename only).
- User cancellation is also a hard delete: `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel)` calls `store.delete_booking`, and the docstring reads "Cancel (delete, AD-13)". It is allowed only before the booking ends (`:359-360`, `booking_to_cancel`). The current-versus-removed question therefore comes down to whether the row exists.

**Not checked:** the body of `check_slot` and migration 0004's contents. I read 9 of the 15 budgeted files, all through git at 9184f9d; nothing was run.

## Digest: how a booking's lifecycle, its end and its removal are tested @ 9184f9d

### How the tests control time and "now"
- **Load-bearing:** nothing in the tests freezes or fakes the clock. No test uses freezegun or patches `utc_now`. The bookings test file states this as its policy: "Times are relative to the real clock: the close-room trigger uses SQLite's own "now"." See `tests/test_bookings.py:3` (module docstring) @ 9184f9d. The only `monkeypatch` uses in tests set env vars and one rooms-service helper (`tests/conftest.py:28-29` db_path; `tests/test_people_web.py:90`; `tests/test_rooms.py:240`) @ 9184f9d.
- **Load-bearing:** the code has two separate clocks.
  - Python takes "now" from `datetime.now(UTC)`: `roombooker/core/time.py:15-17` (utc_now) @ 9184f9d.
  - The room-close trigger compares `start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')`: `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:86-92` (upgrade, rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings) @ 9184f9d.
  - Faking the Python clock would not move SQLite's clock. That is the reason the docstring gives for using the real clock.
- Future dates are always worked out from the real UK date:
  - `uk_day(n)` = `uk.uk_now().date() + n days`: `tests/test_bookings.py:32-33` (uk_day) @ 9184f9d. The `book` fixture defaults to `uk_day(1)` at 10:00 for 60 minutes: `tests/test_bookings.py:68-86` (book) @ 9184f9d.
  - The same pattern appears in `tests/test_calendar.py:30,42,66,81`, `tests/test_demo.py:46`, `tests/e2e/test_book_a_room.py:20,58` and `tests/e2e/test_my_bookings.py:20` @ 9184f9d.
- Past or far-future bookings skip the service and are written straight into the SQLite file:
  - The `insert_booking` fixture does this "for times the web refuses (past, far ahead)": `tests/test_bookings.py:323-335` (insert_booking) @ 9184f9d.
  - Inline raw inserts do the same: `tests/test_bookings.py:279-284` and `:244-253` @ 9184f9d.
  - Fixed past dates (2020-01-07, 2020-01-01, 2026-07-07) are used as "ended" bookings, and fixed future dates (2027, 2030) for DST and trigger cases.
- `test_feed` builds its 30-day window from `uk.utc_now()` minus 31 or 29 days, which is a real-clock offset: `tests/test_feed.py:75-83` (test_subscribed_feed_has_organised_and_attended_bookings_only) @ 9184f9d.
- The only fixed clock is in a database-free formatter test, `STAMP = datetime(2026, 11, 13, 8, 30, tzinfo=UTC)`, passed to `ical.calendar` as a parameter: `tests/test_ical.py:10,36` @ 9184f9d.
- Harness:
  - Each test gets a temporary SQLite file migrated to head through Alembic: `tests/conftest.py:19-33` (migrate_to_head, db_path) @ 9184f9d.
  - The app is driven with `TestClient(create_app(), follow_redirects=False)`: `tests/conftest.py:65-68` (client) @ 9184f9d.
  - The current person is set with the `person_id` cookie: `tests/test_bookings.py:42-47` (act) @ 9184f9d.
  - The e2e tests run one Alembic + seed + uvicorn subprocess per session against a temporary database: `tests/e2e/conftest.py:59-90` (live_server) @ 9184f9d. README describes the two suites at `README.md:112-117` (Tests) @ 9184f9d.

### Lifecycle stages and the tests that cover them
- **Create (book).** Covered through the web:
  - Happy path with attendees: `tests/test_bookings.py:143-166` (test_book_with_attendees_and_details_for_everyone) @ 9184f9d.
  - Refusals, each keeping the typed form (status code shown, message, where it is checked):

    | Case | Status | Message | Checked at |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Overlap | 409 | "Someone has already booked…" | – |
    | In the past | 422 | `IN_THE_PAST` | – |
    | More than 90 days ahead | 422 | `TOO_FAR_AHEAD` | – |
    | Off the quarter hour | 422 | `NOT_ON_QUARTER` | – |
    | Length 255 or 0 | 422 | `BAD_LENGTH` | – |
    | Blank title | 422 | `NEEDS_TITLE` | – |
    | Closed room | 409 | "Attic is closed…" | `tests/test_bookings.py:184-212` (test_refused_bookings_keep_the_form) @ 9184f9d |

  - Concurrent same-slot booking: two threads behind a Barrier call `service.book`, and exactly one gets `BookingConflict`: `tests/test_bookings.py:215-238` (test_two_people_booking_the_same_slot_at_once) @ 9184f9d.
  - **Load-bearing:** database backstop. Raw INSERT and UPDATE are refused with `booking_conflict`, and an insert into a closed room with `room_closed`: `tests/test_bookings.py:241-253` (test_database_refuses_overlaps_and_closed_rooms) @ 9184f9d.
- **Removal by the organiser cancelling.** **Load-bearing:** `tests/test_bookings.py:256-273` (test_only_the_organiser_cancels) @ 9184f9d checks:
  - A non-organiser (even the room's office manager) gets 403 on GET and on POST, with `ONLY_ORGANISER`.
  - The organiser gets the confirmation page, then POST → 303 to `/rooms?notice=cancelled`.
  - Both the `bookings` and `booking_attendees` rows are gone, and the details page returns 404.
  - The slot can be booked again.

  - It leaves the feed: `tests/test_feed.py:113-119` (test_cancelled_booking_leaves_the_feed) @ 9184f9d.
  - Its `.ics` download returns 404: `tests/test_bookings.py:566-572` (test_add_to_calendar_unknown_or_cancelled_booking_is_404) @ 9184f9d.
  - A reused id gets a different UID: `tests/test_feed.py:240-250` (test_reused_booking_id_gets_a_different_uid) @ 9184f9d. It asserts `again == first`, relying on SQLite reusing the highest rowid.
  - e2e cancel through the browser: `tests/e2e/test_book_a_room.py:15-52` (test_find_book_and_cancel) @ 9184f9d.
- **Removal by closing the room.** **Load-bearing:** `tests/test_bookings.py:276-291` (test_closing_a_room_cancels_its_future_bookings) @ 9184f9d:
  - It books one future booking and raw-inserts a 2020 booking, then a manager closes the room.
  - Only the 2020 row survives, its attendees are deleted, and the future booking's page returns 404. This exercises the trigger against SQLite's real "now".

  Related tests:
  - Feed side effect: `tests/test_feed.py:122-131` (test_closing_a_room_removes_its_bookings_from_the_feed) @ 9184f9d.
  - The confirmation text says "its future bookings are cancelled": `tests/test_rooms.py:164-190` (test_close_after_confirmation_then_reopen) @ 9184f9d. This test has no bookings, so it checks the text and the open/closed status only.
  - e2e close and reopen with no bookings: `tests/e2e/test_manage_rooms.py:69` @ 9184f9d.
- **Ended bookings, read-only behaviour.**
  - Ended bookings still show "Book again": `tests/test_bookings.py:338-349` (test_book_again_link_only_for_the_organiser) @ 9184f9d.
  - Ended bookings still show "Add to calendar": `tests/test_bookings.py:526-534` (test_add_to_calendar_writes_a_bst_booking_in_utc) @ 9184f9d.
  - "Book again" from an ended booking whose new time is no longer valid (still past, more than 90 days, a time the clocks skip): `tests/test_bookings.py:432-452` (test_book_again_time_no_longer_valid) @ 9184f9d.
  - "Book again" on a room closed after the booking: `tests/test_bookings.py:455-466` (test_book_again_room_closed) @ 9184f9d.
  - Feed keeps bookings that ended 29 days ago and drops those that ended 31 days ago (`FEED_DAYS_BACK = 30`): `tests/test_feed.py:68-92` @ 9184f9d; `roombooker/bookings/service.py:33,288-290` @ 9184f9d.
- **Seed and demo data.** Demo bookings fill this week and next (Mon–Fri) and a rerun adds none: `tests/test_demo.py:39-64` @ 9184f9d.

### Checks on the removal path that reject a request
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:356-358` (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d rejects a non-organiser with `NotAllowed(ONLY_ORGANISER)`. This is tested.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360` (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d rejects cancelling once `end_at <= utc_now()`, with `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` ("That booking has already ended."). **Load-bearing:** no test covers this.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:88-92` @ 9184f9d deletes only rows with `start_at > now`, and only when `is_closed` goes from false to true. The "past booking kept" side is tested; the boundaries are not (see below).

### Searched for and not found (git grep over `tests` @ 9184f9d)
- **Cancelling an ended booking.** No test refers to `ALREADY_ENDED` or "already ended", and no test cancels a booking inserted in the past (grep `ALREADY_ENDED|already (ended|over|finished)|has ended`: no matches in tests).
- **A booking in progress** (started but not ended):
  - No test closes a room during one. The trigger's `start_at > now` would keep it, and that is untested.
  - No test cancels one.
  - Grep `in progress`: no matches.
- **Reopening a room does not bring bookings back.** Not asserted (grep `reopen.*book`: none).
- **Closing an already closed room** (the trigger's `NOT OLD.is_closed` guard): no test.
- **`upcoming_bookings`** (the organiser's not-yet-ended list, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205` @ 9184f9d): no test mentions it (grep `upcoming`: none). I did not trace which route uses it.
- **Clock control.** No freezegun, `time_machine` or monkeypatch of `utc_now` or `uk_now` anywhere in `tests/`.
- **Boundaries at "now".** No test sits exactly on the cancel cut-off or the trigger cut-off. All times are a day or more away from the real clock.
- **Dependence on the wall clock.** Tests that add days to "today" (`uk_day(85)` with "+7 > 90", `uk_day(89)`, the e2e "next week" check at `tests/e2e/test_my_bookings.py:46`) depend on the real date. Fixed 2027 dates are used for the DST cases.

**Budget.** I read 15 files: the 7 test files, the e2e conftest and 3 e2e test files, README, the 0003 migration, `core/time.py` (grep only) and `bookings/service.py` (excerpts). Not read:
- the rest of `tests/test_rooms.py`, `tests/e2e/test_manage_rooms.py` past line 100, `tests/e2e/test_book_a_room.py` past line 90, and `tests/e2e/test_my_bookings.py` past line 50
- `bookings/store.py` (`delete_booking`, `upcoming_for_organiser`) and `bookings/web.py`, to see how `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` maps to an HTTP status
- `pyproject.toml:27`

Cancelling is a hard delete, and the attendee rows go with the booking through the cascade.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:353-361 (booking_to_cancel)` @ 5f72d52: only the organiser can cancel (`ONLY_ORGANISER`), and only while `end_at > utc_now()` (`ALREADY_ENDED`, line 46). A booking whose `end_at` has passed is never deleted by the app. It stays as history.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56` @ 5f72d52: a booking has only `start_at` and `end_at`, plus `ck_bookings_end_after_start`. There is no status or cancelled-at column. - **Load-bearing:** `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings)` @ 5f72d52: closing a room runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE room_id = NEW.id AND start_at > now`, using SQLite's own clock. So "cancelled" means deleted in this path too.
- `roombooker/bookings/ical.py:52-64 (uid)` @ d7c6ceb comes from `d7c6ceb "feat(calendar): private calendar feed per person, with reset on My bookings"`. The UID scheme it replaced, `booking-{id}@roombooker`, came from `1f90dba "feat(bookings): add "Add to calendar" .ics download to a booking's details page"`. Nothing here was rethought; it adapts to the existing delete model. `bookings.id` is a plain `Integer primary_key` with no AUTOINCREMENT (`0003_bookings.py:40`), so SQLite can reuse the id after a delete. It is the only cited line not from the squash.

No pull requests: every commit cited is either the parentless squash or a direct commit on the local `my-changes` branch, and I made no `gh` lookups.

**Rationale found**

- `docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md` (in 5f72d52):
  - "its bookings that have not started yet are deleted (cancelled, as AD-13 defines cancelling)". It confirms AD-13 equates cancel with delete but doesn't say why.
  - The user settled it on 2026-11-12: "closing a room cancels its future bookings".
  - The delete lives in a trigger, not in `rooms.service`, because of the one-way service dependencies ("AD-1"). It also wins any race: a booking that commits first gets deleted, and one that commits after the close is refused by the closed-room trigger ("AD-4").
  - Trade-offs it accepts: a second writer of `bookings` (against "AD-3"); "The cancelled bookings are not logged one by one: only the close is logged"; it uses the database clock, so a fake clock in tests can't move it.
  - Revisit condition: "if retention (OQ-3) asks for cancelled bookings to be kept". This is the only text in the repo that admits the cancelled-status alternative exists, and it marks that alternative as deferred to an open question, not rejected.
- `ical.py:53-54` docstring and the d7c6ceb message: the hash covers room, times and title "so a booking id SQLite reuses after a delete is a new event, never an update of the old."
- `store.py:119` and `service.py:365` cite "AD-13" and nothing more.

**Decisions shown being made**

- **Closing a room deletes its future bookings, in a trigger rather than Python service code.** This was chosen over code in `rooms.service` or a route calling both services, because of the dependency direction and to win races. Recorded in 5f72d52, in the ADR above.
- **Event UIDs carry a content hash** (`d7c6ceb`). This was chosen over the bare `booking-{id}` UID from `1f90dba`, because a deleted booking's id can be reused. This decision accepts the delete model; it doesn't revisit it.
- **Cancel as delete, not as a recorded state (AD-13).** The history doesn't show this decision being made. It predates the squash and isn't recoverable here.

**Budget:** 3 of 10 commits followed (`5f72d52`, `1f90dba`, `d7c6ceb`); `36d0004` touched `service.py` but none of the cited lines. History stopped at the squash, so the remaining budget went unused. What's left is to read the `greenfield-done` tag and find the commits that introduced `cancel`, `delete_booking`, the cascade and the close trigger, plus the planning-doc text for AD-13 and OQ-3. That needs either a fetch of the tag, which writes to `.git`, or approval for `gh api` reads on the origin repository.

# Codebase research: booking lifecycle and end

This document describes how bookings end in room-booker at commit `9184f9d`, and what reads or depends on that. It is for whoever plans the next change and for anyone checking a single claim. Every claim cites a line or a commit. It recommends nothing.

## Questions

1. (how) How does a booking stop being active today? What marks its end (end time, cancellation, deletion, anything else), and which code paths and database triggers produce each one?
2. (what touches) What reads a booking's end time, or depends on a booking existing or being removed? This covers listings, calendar views, the iCal download and feed, overlap checks, room closing, and seed/demo data.
3. (how) How do the overlap triggers (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`) and the trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` decide which bookings count, for example past vs future and current vs removed?
4. (why) Why is the end of a booking represented the way it is, for example as a delete rather than a recorded state?
5. (how) How are a booking's lifecycle, its end, and its removal tested?

Researchers ran as fresh subagents given only these questions. They were Claude Code subagent types, which may load the repository's `AGENTS.md`; nothing in that file names the work in progress.

## 1. How a booking stops being active

A booking has no status, cancelled or soft-delete column. It is a row with `id`, `room_id`, `organiser_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at`, the times stored as UTC text (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`). The schema adds `CheckConstraint("end_at > start_at")` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). A booking stops being active in one of three ways. Deactivating a person is not one of them.

**1a. Its end time passes. Nothing is written.** "Ended" is computed at read time by comparing `end_at` with `core.time.utc_now()`:

- The upcoming list filters on `end_at > after`, with `after = utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`).
- The details page sets `has_ended = booking.end_at <= uk.utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/web.py:257 (booking_details) @ 9184f9d`). The template hides Cancel unless `booking.can_cancel and not has_ended` (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:34 @ 9184f9d`).
- The service refuses to cancel once `end_at <= utc_now()` and raises `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; the message is at `roombooker/bookings/service.py:46 (ALREADY_ENDED) @ 9184f9d`).
- The feed includes only bookings that end after now minus 30 days (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:285-290 (feed_calendar) @ 9184f9d`).

Ended bookings stay in the table indefinitely. A search for `delete(` and `DELETE FROM` across `*.py` found no purge or expiry, only the two delete paths below.

**1b. The organiser cancels. Python deletes the row.**

- `GET /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:299-314 (confirm_cancel) @ 9184f9d` calls `service.booking_to_cancel` and renders the confirm form (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:22-29 @ 9184f9d`).
- `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:317-322 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` redirects with 303 to `/rooms?notice=cancelled`.
  - `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` (docstring: "Cancel (delete, AD-13)") runs these steps in order:
    1. `booking_to_cancel`
    2. `store.begin_immediate` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:35-42 (begin_immediate) @ 9184f9d`)
    3. `store.delete_booking` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`, which runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE id=…`)
    4. commit, then a log line

Checks on this path that reject a request:

- `_get_row` raises `BookingNotFound` (404, "It may have been cancelled") when the id is missing or out of range (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:267-271 (_get_row) @ 9184f9d`).
- A non-organiser gets `NotAllowed(ONLY_ORGANISER)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:356-358 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; `roombooker/bookings/service.py:93-95 (can_cancel_booking) @ 9184f9d`).
- An ended booking gets `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`). A booking that has started but not ended can still be cancelled.
- The ended check runs before `begin_immediate`, outside the write lock (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:366-367 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`).

Attendee rows go with the booking through `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `booking_attendees.booking_id` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). The cascade depends on `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, which every connection sets (`roombooker/core/db.py:12-16 (PRAGMAS) @ 9184f9d`).

**1c. A manager closes the room. A database trigger deletes its bookings that have not started.**

- `roombooker/rooms/web.py:213-217 (close_room) @ 9184f9d` handles the POST, after a GET confirm page (`roombooker/rooms/web.py:202-210 (confirm_close) @ 9184f9d`).
  - `roombooker/rooms/service.py:215-218 (close_room) @ 9184f9d` calls `_set_closed(..., is_closed=True)` (`roombooker/rooms/service.py:205-212 (_set_closed) @ 9184f9d`). `_require_manager` there rejects anyone who does not manage the room's office.
    - `roombooker/rooms/store.py:49-50 (set_closed) @ 9184f9d` runs `UPDATE rooms SET is_closed=…`, on the column defined at `migrations/versions/0002_rooms.py:31 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`.
      - The trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`) is `AFTER UPDATE OF is_closed ON rooms WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`. It runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE room_id = NEW.id AND start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`.

Python deletes nothing on this path; the `close_room` docstring points to the trigger (`roombooker/rooms/service.py:216-217 (close_room) @ 9184f9d`). The trigger reads SQLite's own `'now'`, whereas paths 1a and 1b read `core.time.utc_now()`, so the code has two separate clocks. Reopening a room restores nothing.

**Not an end path: deactivating a person.** `load_people` marks people missing from the CSV inactive, and its docstring says "Never deletes" (`roombooker/people/store.py:144-174 (load_people) @ 9184f9d`). There is no trigger on `people`. Bookings an inactive person organises or attends stay. The active flag only stops that person being added as an attendee later (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:322-323 (book) @ 9184f9d`).

Looked for at `9184f9d` and not found: any status, cancelled or soft-delete column on bookings; any Python `UPDATE` of bookings (the store has only `insert` and `delete_booking`); any purge of past bookings; any booking delete in `seed.py` or `demo.py`.

## 2. What reads a booking's end time or depends on a booking existing

These are listed by layer. Each entry gives a call site and how it touches the end time or whether the booking exists.

**Schema and database**
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: `start_at` and `end_at` are NOT NULL strings, and CHECK `end_at > start_at` rejects a row whose end is not after its start.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:58-59 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: the only indexes are `(room_id, start_at)` and `(organiser_id)`. No index contains `end_at`.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: attendees cascade on booking delete.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`: the overlap guard reads `start_at` and `end_at` of every booking in the room (see question 3).
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: the close trigger reads `start_at` only, never `end_at`.

**Store queries**
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:45-51 (overlapping) @ 9184f9d`: any room where `start_at < :end AND end_at > :start`.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`: `end_at > after`.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:66-80 (for_person) @ 9184f9d`: the same overlap test, limited to bookings the person organises or attends.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:83-84 (get) @ 9184f9d`: fetch by id. A missing row becomes `BookingNotFound` through `roombooker/bookings/service.py:267-271 (_get_row) @ 9184f9d`.
- `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`: the only Python DELETE on bookings.

**Bookings service**
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:107-120 (check_slot) @ 9184f9d`: computes the end as start plus length. It rejects a start off the quarter hour (`NOT_ON_QUARTER`), a length outside 15–240 minutes or not a multiple of 15 (`BAD_LENGTH`), a start before now unless `allow_past` (`IN_THE_PAST`), and a start more than 90 days ahead (`TOO_FAR_AHEAD`). It does not check the end against now.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:123-148 (free_rooms) @ 9184f9d`: the end comes from `check_slot`, then `store.overlapping` gives the taken rooms. Closed rooms are dropped in Python.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:151-188 (_views) @ 9184f9d`: parses `end_at` into `BookingView.end_at` and sets `can_cancel`. Every path that produces a view goes through here.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:191-197 (bookings_in_slot) @ 9184f9d`: end is start plus length, without `check_slot`, then `store.overlapping`.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`: `upcoming_for_organiser(after=utc_now(), limit=20)`. A booking stays listed until its end passes.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:208-214 (bookings_for_person) @ 9184f9d`: `store.for_person` → `_views`.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d`: an advisory check that the room is closed, then `check_slot`, then an overlap in this room.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:279-282 (booking_calendar) @ 9184f9d`: the single-booking `.ics`, with no ended or closed filter.
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:285-290 (feed_calendar) @ 9184f9d`: bookings for the person overlapping now minus 30 days through `FEED_END` (`9999-12-31T23:59Z`).
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d`: the end comes from `check_slot`, then `begin_immediate` and insert. The trigger aborts map to `RoomClosed`/`BookingConflict` (see question 3).
- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:353-371 (booking_to_cancel, cancel) @ 9184f9d`: the ended check, then the delete (see question 1).

## 3. Which bookings the triggers count

**Overlap guard.** Both `bookings_no_overlap_insert` (BEFORE INSERT) and `bookings_no_overlap_update` (BEFORE UPDATE OF `room_id, start_at, end_at`) run the same `_GUARD` body (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:77-83 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). It makes two checks, in order:

1. If `rooms.is_closed` is true for `NEW.room_id`, it aborts with `room_closed` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`). This runs first, so a booking in a closed room reports `room_closed` even when it also overlaps.
2. If another booking in the same room satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`, it aborts with `booking_conflict`. Intervals are half-open, so back-to-back bookings pass. `other.id IS NOT NEW.id` stops an update colliding with its own row.

The guard has no condition on time or status. It counts every row in the room, past, current and future, so a finished booking still blocks an overlapping new one. A booking stops counting only when it is deleted. Times compare as text, which works because they are stored as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:1-10 (module docstring) @ 9184f9d`). No app code updates `bookings`, so the UPDATE trigger never fires from the app.

**How an abort reaches the user.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d` rolls back an `IntegrityError` and sorts it by substring. `room_closed` becomes `RoomClosed` (409), `booking_conflict` becomes `BookingConflict` (409), and anything else is re-raised. Before the insert, `check_slot` refuses past starts unless `allow_past`, which only demo data passes. So past bookings come from demo data or direct inserts, and the guard still counts them.

**Advisory duplicate.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d` runs the closed check and the same half-open overlap test through `store.overlapping`, filtered to the room in Python. It has no time or status filter either. Its docstring says the triggers remain the guarantee.

**Close trigger.** `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d` fires only when a room goes from open to closed (`WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`), so reopening or re-closing deletes nothing. It deletes rows where `start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`:

- Bookings in progress are kept. So are past bookings, and a booking whose `start_at` equals the current second, because the test is `>`.
- It never reads `end_at`.
- SQLite's `now` carries real seconds while stored values end in `:00Z`. The strings are the same length, so the text comparison holds.

The ADR records the intended rule and the race. A booking that commits first is deleted by the trigger. One that commits after the close is refused by the guard with `room_closed` (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`). The ADR also says the database clock means a fake clock in tests cannot move the trigger (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:7 @ 9184f9d`).

**"Removed" bookings.** There is no column for them. A git grep for `status|cancelled_at|deleted_at|removed` in `roombooker` and `migrations` found only HTTP status codes, the iCal `STATUS:CONFIRMED` line and an unrelated variable. Whether a booking is current or removed depends only on whether its row exists.

## 4. Why the end is represented this way

The history shows what the code does, but not why cancel was made a delete. Every cited line about cancelling and deleting arrives in one parentless commit:

- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel)`, `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking)`, the cascade at `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66`, and the close trigger at `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95` all arrive in `5f72d52 "chore: remove BMad files and the walkthrough log"`.
- That commit's message calls it "the same app with no BMad install, planning documents or run log… The greenfield-done tag keeps them." This clone has no `greenfield-done` tag, so history stops there.

What the repository does record:

- The code cites "AD-13" for cancel as delete and says nothing more (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`). AD-n points to a planning document that no longer exists (`AGENTS.md:29 @ 9184f9d`).
- The room-close ADR says future bookings "are deleted (cancelled, as AD-13 defines cancelling)", following a user decision on 2026-11-12 that "closing a room cancels its future bookings" (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`).
  - The delete sits in a trigger, not in `rooms.service`, because service dependencies run one way ("AD-1") and because a trigger wins the race described in question 3.
  - The ADR names the trade-offs it accepts:
    - a second writer of `bookings` (against "AD-3")
    - "The cancelled bookings are not logged one by one: only the close is logged"
    - the database clock
  - Its revisit condition is "if retention (OQ-3) asks for cancelled bookings to be kept". This is the only text in the repository that mentions keeping cancelled bookings as an alternative, and it leaves that to an open question rather than rejecting it.
- Bookings are the only entity here with no recorded end state. Rooms record `is_closed` (`migrations/versions/0002_rooms.py:31 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`), and people are marked inactive rather than deleted (`roombooker/people/store.py:144-174 (load_people) @ 9184f9d`).
- Later code adapts to the delete model and does not revisit it. `1f90dba "feat(bookings): add "Add to calendar" .ics download to a booking's details page"` introduced UIDs of the form `booking-{id}@roombooker`. `d7c6ceb "feat(calendar): private calendar feed per person, with reset on My bookings"` replaced them with a content hash, because SQLite can reuse a deleted booking's id. `bookings.id` is a plain integer primary key without AUTOINCREMENT (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:40 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`).

No pull requests were found. Every cited commit is either the squash or a direct commit on the local branch.

## 5. How the lifecycle is tested

**Time in tests.**

- Nothing freezes or fakes the clock. `tests/test_bookings.py:3 (module docstring) @ 9184f9d` states the policy: times are relative to the real clock, because the close-room trigger uses SQLite's own "now".

# Codebase research: booking lifecycle and end

This document describes how bookings end in room-booker at commit `9184f9d`, and what reads or depends on that. It is for whoever plans the next change and for anyone checking a single claim. Every claim cites a line or a commit. It recommends nothing.

## Questions

1. (how) How does a booking stop being active today? What marks its end (end time, cancellation, deletion, anything else), and which code paths and database triggers produce each one?
2. (what touches) What reads a booking's end time, or depends on a booking existing or being removed? This covers listings, calendar views, the iCal download and feed, overlap checks, room closing, and seed/demo data.
3. (how) How do the overlap triggers (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`) and the trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` decide which bookings count, for example past vs future and current vs removed?
4. (why) Why is the end of a booking represented the way it is, for example as a delete rather than a recorded state?
5. (how) How are a booking's lifecycle, its end, and its removal tested?

Researchers ran as fresh subagents given only these questions. They were Claude Code subagent types, which may load the repository's `AGENTS.md`; nothing in that file names the work in progress.

## 1. How a booking stops being active

A booking has no status, cancelled or soft-delete column. It is a row with `id`, `room_id`, `organiser_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at`, the times stored as UTC text (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`). The schema adds `CheckConstraint("end_at > start_at")` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). A booking stops being active in one of three ways. Deactivating a person is not one of them.

**1a. Its end time passes. Nothing is written.** "Ended" is computed at read time by comparing `end_at` with `core.time.utc_now()`:

- The upcoming list filters on `end_at > after`, with `after = utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`).
- The details page sets `has_ended = booking.end_at <= uk.utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/web.py:257 (booking_details) @ 9184f9d`). The template hides Cancel unless `booking.can_cancel and not has_ended` (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:34 @ 9184f9d`).
- The service refuses to cancel once `end_at <= utc_now()` and raises `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; the message is at `roombooker/bookings/service.py:46 (ALREADY_ENDED) @ 9184f9d`).
- The feed includes only bookings that end after now minus 30 days (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:285-290 (feed_calendar) @ 9184f9d`).

Ended bookings stay in the table indefinitely. A search for `delete(` and `DELETE FROM` across `*.py` found no purge or expiry, only the two delete paths below.

**1b. The organiser cancels. Python deletes the row.**

- `GET /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:299-314 (confirm_cancel) @ 9184f9d` calls `service.booking_to_cancel` and renders the confirm form (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:22-29 @ 9184f9d`).
- `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:317-322 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` redirects with 303 to `/rooms?notice=cancelled`.
  - `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` (docstring: "Cancel (delete, AD-13)") runs these steps in order:
    1. `booking_to_cancel`
    2. `store.begin_immediate` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:35-42 (begin_immediate) @ 9184f9d`)
    3. `store.delete_booking` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`, which runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE id=…`)
    4. commit, then a log line

Checks on this path that reject a request:

- `_get_row` raises `BookingNotFound` (404, "It may have been cancelled") when the id is missing or out of range (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:267-271 (_get_row) @ 9184f9d`).
- A non-organiser gets `NotAllowed(ONLY_ORGANISER)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:356-358 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; `roombooker/bookings/service.py:93-95 (can_cancel_booking) @ 9184f9d`).
- An ended booking gets `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`). A booking that has started but not ended can still be cancelled.
- The ended check runs before `begin_immediate`, outside the write lock (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:366-367 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`).

Attendee rows go with the booking through `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `booking_attendees.booking_id` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). The cascade depends on `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, which every connection sets (`roombooker/core/db.py:12-16 (PRAGMAS) @ 9184f9d`).

**1c. A manager closes the room. A database trigger deletes its bookings that have not started.**

- `roombooker/rooms/web.py:213-217 (close_room) @ 9184f9d` handles the POST, after a GET confirm page (`roombooker/rooms/web.py:202-210 (confirm_close) @ 9184f9d`).
  - `roombooker/rooms/service.py:215-218 (close_room) @ 9184f9d` calls `_set_closed(..., is_closed=True)` (`roombooker/rooms/service.py:205-212 (_set_closed) @ 9184f9d`). `_require_manager` there rejects anyone who does not manage the room's office.
    - `roombooker/rooms/store.py:49-50 (set_closed) @ 9184f9d` runs `UPDATE rooms SET is_closed=…`, on the column defined at `migrations/versions/0002_rooms.py:31 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`.
      - The trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`) is `AFTER UPDATE OF is_closed ON rooms WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`. It runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE room_id = NEW.id AND start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`.

Python deletes nothing on this path; the `close_room` docstring points to the trigger (`roombooker/rooms/service.py:216-217 (close_room) @ 9184f9d`). The trigger reads SQLite's own `'now'`, whereas paths 1a and 1b read `core.time.utc_now()`, so the code has two separate clocks. Reopening a room restores nothing.

**Not an end path: deactivating a person.** `load_people` marks people missing from the CSV inactive, and its docstring says "Never deletes" (`roombooker/people/store.py:144-174 (load_people) @ 9184f9d`). There is no trigger on `people`. Bookings an inactive person organises or attends stay. The active flag only stops that person being added as an attendee later (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:322-323 (book) @ 9184f9d`).

Looked for at `9184f9d` and not found: any status, cancelled or soft-delete column on bookings; any Python `UPDATE` of bookings (the store has only `insert` and `delete_booking`); any purge of past bookings; any booking delete in `seed.py` or `demo.py`.

## 2. What reads a booking's end time or depends on a booking existing

These are listed by layer. Each entry gives a call site and how it touches the end time or whether the booking exists.

**Schema and database**
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: `start_at` and `end_at` are NOT NULL strings, and CHECK `end_at > start_at` rejects a row whose end is not after its start.
- `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:58-59 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`: the only indexes are `(room_id, start_at)` and `(organiser_id)`. No index contains `end_at`.

1. If `rooms.is_closed` is true for `NEW.room_id`, it aborts with `room_closed` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`). This runs first, so a booking in a closed room reports `room_closed` even when it also overlaps.
2. If another booking in the same room satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`, it aborts with `booking_conflict`. Intervals are half-open, so back-to-back bookings pass. `other.id IS NOT NEW.id` stops an update colliding with its own row.

The guard has no condition on time or status. It counts every row in the room, past, current and future, so a finished booking still blocks an overlapping new one. A booking stops counting only when it is deleted. Times compare as text, which works because they are stored as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:1-10 (module docstring) @ 9184f9d`). No app code updates `bookings`, so the UPDATE trigger never fires from the app.

**How an abort reaches the user.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d` rolls back an `IntegrityError` and sorts it by substring. `room_closed` becomes `RoomClosed` (409), `booking_conflict` becomes `BookingConflict` (409), and anything else is re-raised. Before the insert, `check_slot` refuses past starts unless `allow_past`, which only demo data passes. So past bookings come from demo data or direct inserts, and the guard still counts them.

**Advisory duplicate.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d` runs the closed check and the same half-open overlap test through `store.overlapping`, filtered to the room in Python. - Bookings in progress are kept. So are past bookings, and a booking whose `start_at` equals the current second, because the test is `>`.
- It never reads `end_at`.
- SQLite's `now` carries real seconds while stored values end in `:00Z`. The strings are the same length, so the text comparison holds.

The ADR records the intended rule and the race. A booking that commits first is deleted by the trigger. One that commits after the close is refused by the guard with `room_closed` (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`). The ADR also says the database clock means a fake clock in tests cannot move the trigger (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:7 @ 9184f9d`).

**"Removed" bookings.** There is no column for them. # Codebase research: booking lifecycle and end

This document describes how bookings end in room-booker at commit `9184f9d`, and what reads or depends on that. It is for whoever plans the next change and for anyone checking a single claim. Every claim cites a line or a commit. It recommends nothing.

## Questions

1. (how) How does a booking stop being active today? What marks its end (end time, cancellation, deletion, anything else), and which code paths and database triggers produce each one?
2. (what touches) What reads a booking's end time, or depends on a booking existing or being removed? This covers listings, calendar views, the iCal download and feed, overlap checks, room closing, and seed/demo data.
3. (how) How do the overlap triggers (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`) and the trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` decide which bookings count, for example past vs future and current vs removed?
4. (why) Why is the end of a booking represented the way it is, for example as a delete rather than a recorded state?
5. (how) How are a booking's lifecycle, its end, and its removal tested?

Researchers ran as fresh subagents given only these questions. They were Claude Code subagent types, which may load the repository's `AGENTS.md`; nothing in that file names the work in progress.

## 1. How a booking stops being active

A booking has no status, cancelled or soft-delete column. It is a row with `id`, `room_id`, `organiser_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at`, the times stored as UTC text (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`). The schema adds `CheckConstraint("end_at > start_at")` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). A booking stops being active in one of three ways. Deactivating a person is not one of them.

**1a. Its end time passes. Nothing is written.** "Ended" is computed at read time by comparing `end_at` with `core.time.utc_now()`:

- The upcoming list filters on `end_at > after`, with `after = utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`).
- The details page sets `has_ended = booking.end_at <= uk.utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/web.py:257 (booking_details) @ 9184f9d`). The template hides Cancel unless `booking.can_cancel and not has_ended` (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:34 @ 9184f9d`).
- The service refuses to cancel once `end_at <= utc_now()` and raises `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; the message is at `roombooker/bookings/service.py:46 (ALREADY_ENDED) @ 9184f9d`).
- The feed includes only bookings that end after now minus 30 days (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:285-290 (feed_calendar) @ 9184f9d`).

Ended bookings stay in the table indefinitely. A search for `delete(` and `DELETE FROM` across `*.py` found no purge or expiry, only the two delete paths below.

**1b. The organiser cancels. Python deletes the row.**

- `GET /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:299-314 (confirm_cancel) @ 9184f9d` calls `service.booking_to_cancel` and renders the confirm form (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:22-29 @ 9184f9d`).
- `POST /bookings/{id}/cancel`: `roombooker/bookings/web.py:317-322 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` redirects with 303 to `/rooms?notice=cancelled`.
  - `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d` (docstring: "Cancel (delete, AD-13)") runs these steps in order:
    1. `booking_to_cancel`
    2. `store.begin_immediate` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:35-42 (begin_immediate) @ 9184f9d`)
    3. `store.delete_booking` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`, which runs `DELETE FROM bookings WHERE id=…`)
    4. commit, then a log line

Checks on this path that reject a request:

- `_get_row` raises `BookingNotFound` (404, "It may have been cancelled") when the id is missing or out of range (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:267-271 (_get_row) @ 9184f9d`).

## 3. Which bookings the triggers count

**Overlap guard.** Both `bookings_no_overlap_insert` (BEFORE INSERT) and `bookings_no_overlap_update` (BEFORE UPDATE OF `room_id, start_at, end_at`) run the same `_GUARD` body (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:77-83 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). It makes two checks, in order:

1. If `rooms.is_closed` is true for `NEW.room_id`, it aborts with `room_closed` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`). This runs first, so a booking in a closed room reports `room_closed` even when it also overlaps.
2. If another booking in the same room satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`, it aborts with `booking_conflict`. Intervals are half-open, so back-to-back bookings pass. `other.id IS NOT NEW.id` stops an update colliding with its own row.

The guard has no condition on time or status. It counts every row in the room, past, current and future, so a finished booking still blocks an overlapping new one. A booking stops counting only when it is deleted. Times compare as text, which works because they are stored as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:1-10 (module docstring) @ 9184f9d`). No app code updates `bookings`, so the UPDATE trigger never fires from the app.

**How an abort reaches the user.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d` rolls back an `IntegrityError` and sorts it by substring. `room_closed` becomes `RoomClosed` (409), `booking_conflict` becomes `BookingConflict` (409), and anything else is re-raised. Before the insert, `check_slot` refuses past starts unless `allow_past`, which only demo data passes. So past bookings come from demo data or direct inserts, and the guard still counts them.

**Advisory duplicate.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d` runs the closed check and the same half-open overlap test through `store.overlapping`, filtered to the room in Python. It has no time or status filter either. Its docstring says the triggers remain the guarantee.

**Close trigger.** `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d` fires only when a room goes from open to closed (`WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`), so reopening or re-closing deletes nothing. It deletes rows where `start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`:

- Bookings in progress are kept. So are past bookings, and a booking whose `start_at` equals the current second, because the test is `>`.
- It never reads `end_at`.
- SQLite's `now` carries real seconds while stored values end in `:00Z`. The strings are the same length, so the text comparison holds.

The ADR records the intended rule and the race. A booking that commits first is deleted by the trigger. One that commits after the close is refused by the guard with `room_closed` (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`). The ADR also says the database clock means a fake clock in tests cannot move the trigger (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:7 @ 9184f9d`).

**"Removed" bookings.** There is no column for them. A git grep for `status|cancelled_at|deleted_at|removed` in `roombooker` and `migrations` found only HTTP status codes, the iCal `STATUS:CONFIRMED` line and an unrelated variable. Whether a booking is current or removed depends only on whether its row exists.

## 4. Why the end is represented this way

The history shows what the code does, but not why cancel was made a delete. Every cited line about cancelling and deleting arrives in one parentless commit:

- `roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel)`, `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking)`, the cascade at `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:65-66`, and the close trigger at `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95` all arrive in `5f72d52 "chore: remove BMad files and the walkthrough log"`.
- That commit's message calls it "the same app with no BMad install, planning documents or run log… The greenfield-done tag keeps them." This clone has no `greenfield-done` tag, so history stops there.

What the repository does record:

- The code cites "AD-13" for cancel as delete and says nothing more (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/store.py:118-120 (delete_booking) @ 9184f9d`). AD-n points to a planning document that no longer exists (`AGENTS.md:29 @ 9184f9d`).
- The room-close ADR says future bookings "are deleted (cancelled, as AD-13 defines cancelling)", following a user decision on 2026-11-12 that "closing a room cancels its future bookings" (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`).
  - The delete sits in a trigger, not in `rooms.service`, because service dependencies run one way ("AD-1") and because a trigger wins the race described in question 3.
  - The ADR names the trade-offs it accepts:
    - a second writer of `bookings` (against "AD-3")
    - "The cancelled bookings are not logged one by one: only the close is logged"
    - the database clock
  - Its revisit condition is "if retention (OQ-3) asks for cancelled bookings to be kept". This is the only text in the repository that mentions keeping cancelled bookings as an alternative, and it leaves that to an open question rather than rejecting it.
- Bookings are the only entity here with no recorded end state. Rooms record `is_closed` (`migrations/versions/0002_rooms.py:31 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`), and people are marked inactive rather than deleted (`roombooker/people/store.py:144-174 (load_people) @ 9184f9d`).
- Later code adapts to the delete model and does not revisit it. `1f90dba "feat(bookings): add "Add to calendar" .ics download to a booking's details page"` introduced UIDs of the form `booking-{id}@roombooker`. `d7c6ceb "feat(calendar): private calendar feed per person, with reset on My bookings"` replaced them with a content hash, because SQLite can reuse a deleted booking's id. `bookings.id` is a plain integer primary key without AUTOINCREMENT (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:40 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`).

No pull requests were found. Every cited commit is either the squash or a direct commit on the local branch.

## 5. How the lifecycle is tested

**Time in tests.**

+## 3. Which bookings the triggers count
+
+**Overlap guard.** Both `bookings_no_overlap_insert` (BEFORE INSERT) and `bookings_no_overlap_update` (BEFORE UPDATE OF `room_id, start_at, end_at`) run the same `_GUARD` body (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:77-83 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). It makes two checks, in order:
+
+1. If `rooms.is_closed` is true for `NEW.room_id`, it aborts with `room_closed` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:23-34 (_GUARD) @ 9184f9d`). This runs first, so a booking in a closed room reports `room_closed` even when it also overlaps.
+2. If another booking in the same room satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at`, it aborts with `booking_conflict`. Intervals are half-open, so back-to-back bookings pass. `other.id IS NOT NEW.id` stops an update colliding with its own row.
+
+The guard has no condition on time or status. It counts every row in the room, past, current and future, so a finished booking still blocks an overlapping new one. A booking stops counting only when it is deleted. Times compare as text, which works because they are stored as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:1-10 (module docstring) @ 9184f9d`). No app code updates `bookings`, so the UPDATE trigger never fires from the app.
+
+**How an abort reaches the user.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:302-350 (book) @ 9184f9d` rolls back an `IntegrityError` and sorts it by substring. `room_closed` becomes `RoomClosed` (409), `booking_conflict` becomes `BookingConflict` (409), and anything else is re-raised. Before the insert, `check_slot` refuses past starts unless `allow_past`, which only demo data passes. So past bookings come from demo data or direct inserts, and the guard still counts them.
+
+**Advisory duplicate.** `roombooker/bookings/service.py:225-240 (slot_problem) @ 9184f9d` runs the closed check and the same half-open overlap test through `store.overlapping`, filtered to the room in Python. It has no time or status filter either. Its docstring says the triggers remain the guarantee.
+
+**Close trigger.** `migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d` fires only when a room goes from open to closed (`WHEN NEW.is_closed AND NOT OLD.is_closed`), so reopening or re-closing deletes nothing. It deletes rows where `start_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')`:
+
+- Bookings in progress are kept. So are past bookings, and a booking whose `start_at` equals the current second, because the test is `>`.
+- It never reads `end_at`.
+- SQLite's `now` carries real seconds while stored values end in `:00Z`. The strings are the same length, so the text comparison holds.
+
+The ADR records the intended rule and the race. A booking that commits first is deleted by the trigger. One that commits after the close is refused by the guard with `room_closed` (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:3 @ 9184f9d`). The ADR also says the database clock means a fake clock in tests cannot move the trigger (`docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md:7 @ 9184f9d`).
+
+**"Removed" bookings.** There is no column for them. A git grep for `status|cancelled_at|deleted_at|removed` in `roombooker` and `migrations` found only HTTP status codes, the iCal `STATUS:CONFIRMED` line and an unrelated variable. Whether a booking is current or removed depends only on whether its row exists.

+- **Reopening a room.** No test asserts that reopening restores no bookings.
+- **Closing an already-closed room**, the trigger's `NOT OLD.is_closed` guard. No test.
+- **`upcoming_bookings`.** No test mentions it by name.
+- **Boundaries at "now".** All times are at least a day from the real clock.
+
+## Where the answers meet
+
+- **`roombooker/bookings/service.py:353-361 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`** is reached from questions 1, 2 and 5. It is the only Python check on time at the end of a booking: it rejects `end_at <= utc_now()` with `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)`, and rejects non-organisers with `NotAllowed(ONLY_ORGANISER)`. No test covers the ended branch.

# Codebase verifier

You check claims someone else made, from what you open rather than from their wording; you start fresh so the researcher's reading cannot become yours. The brief (the commit, the validation level, the paths to leave out) and a batch of ledger lines, `ref=[n] status=... kind=<code|history> — <claim with its citation>`, are in your message; project instructions, branch or folder names and file status your harness loaded are not your brief.

Open only through git at the commit, never your harness's file or search tools or `git status`, which see the working tree (`git show <commit>:<path> | cat -n`, `git grep -n <pattern> <commit> -- <paths>`, `git show <sha>`, `gh pr view <number>`), with the excluded paths left out. For a code claim, read the cited lines and judge whether they say what the claim says; when what it describes sits at other lines of that commit, re-anchor it by its symbol and judge those; at validation `max`, when the claim says what code calls or depends on, follow one more edge and judge again. For a history claim, open the commit and its pull request.

Reply with a digest: per `ref`, the citation as it should read (same form; for code, the symbol without parentheses and the brief's short commit) and one verdict: `verified`; `disputed` when the code bears out only part, saying which; `overturned` when it says otherwise, saying what, cited; `unverified` when what you can open does not settle it.

## Decisions found

**Calendar event UIDs carry a content hash beside the booking id.** `d7c6ceb "feat(calendar): private calendar feed per person, with reset on My bookings"` changed the UID from `booking-{id}@roombooker` (introduced in `1f90dba "feat(bookings): add "Add to calendar" .ics download to a booking's details page"`) to `booking-{id}-{hash}@roombooker`, hashing room, start, end and title (`roombooker/bookings/ical.py:52-64 (uid) @ 9184f9d`). The rationale in its docstring and commit message is "so a booking id SQLite reuses after a delete is a new event, never an update of the old." `bookings.id` has no AUTOINCREMENT (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:40 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`).

- *Hard to reverse:* subscribed calendars key events by UID, so changing the scheme again re-creates every event in every subscriber's calendar.
- *Surprising without context:* any change to a booking's room, times or title yields a new UID, so calendars see it as a delete plus an add rather than an update.
- *A real trade-off:* stable per-booking identity was given up to avoid a reused id updating someone else's old event.

Proposed ADR: `docs/decisions/adr-calendar-uids-hash-booking-content.md`. User's answer: pending.
EOF
